newsitem.title: SPAIN: Aznar vows to intensify fight against ETA.
newsitem.headline: Aznar vows to intensify fight against ETA.

text.p: Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar vowed on Monday to intensify the fight against Basque separatist guerrillas after the killing of a young Spanish politician, pledging "We will put a stop to terrorism."

But in his first public comments since the death on Sunday of 29-year-old Miguel Angel Blanco, Aznar warned the Spanish people in a nationally televised address of "painful days" ahead in the struggle against the rebel group ETA.

"It is the responsibility of the prime minister to use all means within our reach to strengthen all points of agreement and unity among the democratic forces in response to Herri Batasuna and the terrorists," Aznar said.
Aznar promised to speed up the implementation of anti-terrorist legislation and said he knew there was room for improvement in the fight against ETA and its political arm Herri Batasuna.
Although he did not give any specifics, he said further measures could be announced later on Monday.

Blanco, a Basque town councillor, was found on Saturday bound and bloodied, two bullets lodged in his brain, about 48 hours after ETA guerrillas kidnapped him. He died early on Sunday in a hospital in the Basque city of San Sebastian.
"Those who only know how to kill, those who only know how to kidnap, will continue doing it," Aznar said from the steps of the prime minister's residence in Madrid.
But he urged Spaniards to maintain solidarity.
"Without a doubt, we are going to win. Without a doubt, we will put a stop to terrorism," he promised.
Aznar lashed out angrily at Herri Batasuna members, calling them "accomplices" to murder and urging Spaniards to isolate them.
